name: Kukulkan

domain_history.domain: Yucatec Maya feathered-serpent deity, concentrated at Chichén Itzá and later Mayapán — a Postclassic, Yucatec-regional phenomenon, NOT a pan-Maya, all-periods deity like Itzamna

notes: The feathered-serpent motif itself predates both Maya and Aztec civilizations (Olmec iconography, c. 1600-400 BCE; Teotihuacan's Temple of the Feathered Serpent, c. 150-600 CE) — a pan-Mesoamerican regional motif, not independently invented or directly borrowed at the point of Spanish contact by either the Maya or the Mexica. See claim_kukulkan_quetzalcoatl_regional_network for the documented Epiclassic-period religious-network diffusion (Ringle, Gallareta Negrón, and Bey 1998) that explains Kukulkan's relationship to central-Mexican Quetzalcoatl worship.
